steps.title: Last option: Powerwash
instructions: A Powerwash erases everything saved on this Chromebook and puts it back to factory settings.
It removes files in your Downloads folder, saved Wi-Fi networks, and settings. Files in Google Drive are safe.
After a Powerwash you must sign in again, and your Chromebook may need to reconnect to your school's management. This is called re-enrollment.
A Powerwash is NOT the same as a hardware reset. A hardware reset only restarts the hardware. A Powerwash erases the Chromebook.
steps.warning: A Powerwash cannot be undone. If you are not sure, answer No and get help from a technician instead.
steps.question: Do you want to continue with a Powerwash?

steps.title: Save your files first
instructions: Drag any files you need into Google Drive (on the left side of the Files app).
steps.warning: Anything left in Downloads or My files will be erased by the Powerwash.
steps.question: Are your important files saved in Google Drive, or do you have no files to save?

steps.title: Make sure you can sign back in
instructions: After a Powerwash you need an internet connection to sign in.
You also need your full school email address and password.
steps.question: Are you connected to Wi-Fi, and do you know your school email and password?

steps.title: Run the Powerwash
instructions: On the sign-in screen, press and hold Ctrl + Alt + Shift + R.
In the box that appears, click Powerwash, then click Continue.
If you do not see a Powerwash option, or it says Powerwash is not allowed, stop and answer No.
steps.warning: This erases everything saved on this Chromebook. Files in Google Drive are safe.
steps.question: Did the Chromebook restart and show a welcome or sign-in screen?

steps.title: Sign back in
instructions: Sign in with your full school email address and password.
If the Chromebook says it is being enrolled or managed by your school, wait for it to finish.
If it asks for information you don't have, or shows an error, stop. Do not try to get past that screen.
steps.question: Did you sign in, and is the original problem fixed?
